text:
maya: sharing the new mock for autoscaling controls — focused on min/max, burst toggle, GPU pool selector, and the SLO slider. screenshot: https://redwood.mock/s/asc-v3.png jon: nice! layout looks cleaner. quick note: min/max inputs feel crowded next to the slider. can we stack them vertically on narrow screens? tara: +1 to stacking. also we should show units (GPUs) explicitly on the inputs, not just the label. samir: regarding burst: is that a temporary throttle above max or an override to autoscale? i worry customers will think it increases steady-state capacity. maya: burst is intended as short-lived headroom (configurable duration). thinking of a tooltip: "Burst: allow short-term capacity above max for spikes (duration controls how long)." open to wording. anna: customer asked for a "cost saver" preset that sets min=0, max=2, burst=enabled but short (30s). worth adding presets? :star: jon: presets are good — maybe show them as chips at the top: "Presets: Balanced / Cost saver / Latency first". chip copy: use sentence case. liam: accessibility nits: color contrast on the SLO slider thumb is failing AA when using the current teal on pale bg. rachel can you confirm recommended token color? rachel: confirm — slider thumb needs contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 for small UI controls. use #005b8a or a darker variant. also ensure keyboard focus ring is visible (2px outline + offset). jon: copy tweak for the SLO label: current "SLO" is too techy for some PMs. suggestion: "Latency target (p99)" with a tooltip: "Target p99 tail latency to maintain". samir: another thought: GPU pool selection — currently a long list. can we surface recommended pools based on model footprint and region? e.g., "Recommended: gpu-large-east-1 (best perf)" with an explain icon. maya: yes, we have autosuggest data. display recommended as the first, then group by region. also include an inline badge for "price tier" (low / medium / high). liam: keyboard nav for pool selector: ensure arrow keys move between groups and enter selects. role="listbox" + aria-activedescendant pattern should work. example snippet: ```html
\n
gpu-small-east-1
\n
\n``` rachel: good. also add aria-describedby on the burst control to point at the duration explanation so screen readers read both state + duration. jon: UX question: where do we show guardrail warnings? inline under the control or as a banner at the top? for discoverability i prefer inline near the related field. tara: inline makes sense, but also a compact banner when any guardrail is tripped so users don't miss it after scrolling. maya: plan: inline warnings + a consolidated banner that appears at top of panel if any guardrail violates. banner copy: "One or more guardrails exceeded — review below" — thoughts on phrasing? anna: maybe "Action needed: guardrails exceeded" is clearer for customers who expect an ops task. jon: subtle tone: "Action needed" sounds urgent; maybe only for production accounts. for self-serve keep: "Review guardrail limits". we can conditionally vary tone by account tier. maya: good call. leaving that for product rules later. for this review: tasks: 1) jon: update mock with stacked min/max for <600px and darker slider thumb. 2) liam/rachel: add aria code snippet and verify focus styles. 3) samir: add recommended-pool badge and preset flow. 4) tara: inline warning UI + banner behavior. samir: quick question on metrics: when burst is used, should we attribute cost to the burst label in cost graph or blend into total? ops teams asked for a separate breakdown. maya: separate breakdown preferred — "Burst usage" line in cost/time chart. note for backend. deploy-bot: snapshot created: asc-v3-review-1762003456 at 1762003460 jon: tiny copy nit: change "max capacity" to "max GPUs" in the control label. avoids ambiguity. rachel: and add offscreen text: "{control} is required" on fields that must be populated for form validation. maya: thanks all — i'll update the Figma + write up the acceptance criteria. will ping when ready for a follow-up review. :thumbsup: anna: thanks, team! this will help our mid-market customers a lot. liam: leaving a small perf guard: default burst multiplier shouldn't exceed 2x for now until we have autoscaler tests. noted in ACs. maya: noted. end of thread.
